criterion: The home route runs as one long scroll that opens on a headline with two prominent actions and a product demonstration, then moves through security, three named customers, six capabilities, sector solutions, three templates and three power tools before closing on a call to action.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the home route is one continuous scroll whose order opens on the hero and ends on the closing call to action, with the named stages in between. No when the page is short, the order differs, or a named stage is absent.

criterion: Starting a free trial ends on a confirmation page that reads back the team name the visitor typed and the address of the team site created for them.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the confirmation page shows both the team name and a team site address derived from that name. No when the visitor lands back on the form or the address is absent.

criterion: Every page comparing Sheaf with a competing product shows, beside each factual claim about that product, the source of the claim and the date the claim was checked.
evaluation_rule: Yes when each comparison row carries a visible source and a visible checked date beside the statement. No when a claim stands on its own.

criterion: A sector page carries the sentence that a database structure meets spreadsheet flexibility, and the identical sentence appears on every other sector page.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the shared claim appears word for word on two different sector pages. No when each sector page states the claim in its own wording.

criterion: The header carries five menu triggers reading Product, Solutions, Developers, Resources and Pricing, a star control, a Sign In link and a Sign Up button.
evaluation_rule: Yes when all five triggers, the star control and both actions sit in the header on every route. No when one of the eight is absent.

criterion: An author opening the authoring console sees a table of every route showing its slug, its template, its status and when the route was last edited, and reaches an editor from any row.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the console opens on a route table carrying those four columns and a row leads to an editor. No when the console opens on something else.

criterion: An empty media library states what would appear there and offers the upload action in the same place.
evaluation_rule: Yes when an empty media library names what belongs there and offers an upload action. No when the area renders blank.

criterion: One horizontal gradient running teal on the left to green on the right carries the brand across the full-width section bands, the announcement bar and the closing strip of each menu panel.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a single left to right teal to green gradient carries those three surfaces. No when a second gradient appears anywhere on the site.

criterion: Footer social links are rounded on one diagonal and square on the other, echoing the geometry of the mark in the header.
evaluation_rule: Yes when every footer social link shows the asymmetric rounding the mark uses. No when the links are uniformly rounded or uniformly square.

criterion: Body text on the dark footer, and any text set on the accent teal, both meet the WCAG AA contrast bar.
evaluation_rule: Yes when both pairings sit at or above the AA ratio when measured on the rendered page. No when either pairing sits below.

criterion: Hovering or keyboard-focusing a link grows an underline outward from one side, rather than switching a full-width underline on.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the underline animates its width from one edge on hover and again on keyboard focus. No when the underline appears at full width at once.

criterion: On the home route the first level heading steps down to a smaller size at phone width, and the header halves in height at that width.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the headline renders visibly smaller at phone width than at desktop width and the header is shorter there. No when the headline renders at the same size at both widths.

criterion: Across the home route and every sector route, headings run through six steps down to one body size, the fifth step set in uppercase with open letter spacing as an eyebrow label, and every role sits at a size of its own.
evaluation_rule: Yes when six heading steps and one body size are visible across the site, the eyebrow label is uppercase with open letter spacing, and two roles share a size nowhere. No when the scale collapses to fewer steps or two roles render at one size.

criterion: Every route is operable from the keyboard alone, with a visible focus ring, an Escape key that closes an open menu panel back to the trigger, and a spoken name on every icon-only control.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a keyboard walk of a route reaches every control in visual order, shows focus, closes a panel with Escape, and lands on icon controls that announce a name. No when the walk loses focus, skips a control, or reaches an unnamed icon button.

criterion: Every illustration on the site is drawn by the build itself, comes out identical on a second load, and each capability figure carries a caption saying what a real recording would show.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the artwork is generated, renders the same on a reload, and each capability figure carries its caption. No when a photograph, a logo file or a stock illustration appears, or the artwork shifts between loads.

criterion: The site sells the product and holds none of the product surface, so a grid, a formula editor, an access-rule editor, a form builder, an assistant and a billing screen are all absent, and the sign-in path leaves for the product origin.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a walk of the site finds marketing content only and every way in leads off to the product origin. No when any product surface renders on this origin.

criterion: The home route contacts an advertising or analytics origin on first paint, ahead of the visitor answering the cookie question.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a third-party origin is requested on first paint before any cookie answer is recorded. No when the first paint touches the site origin alone.
